C1.evidence: X1 patch was applied to a fresh 28706dc scratch worktree; 142-input census and named r85 probes replay without either other claim.

C2.reason: D1 and D2 decision tables describe the 28706dc baseline. D2 explicitly marks the C1 integration debt at lines 251-263; its r85-masked table output at lines 243-249 is stale after X1 adds two findings and changes the footer 3 to 5. D1 also states it documents baseline behavior, not C1.

C3.evidence: M1, M2, and M3 patches were independently applied to separate 28706dc archives; each exited CLEAN under both the baseline checker and X1-patched checker. Each cluster has zero entity provenance records, so C1 does not affect its checker tuple.

collisions_and_debt.action: Apply at most one patch; do not stack these alternatives.

collisions_and_debt.action: Choose one, update it to the selected C1 patch's output, and make its named probe inputs replayable; D1/D2 synthetic r87-* inputs are scratch-only and are not in either table patch.

collisions_and_debt.kind: same new fixture paths; mutually exclusive C3 alternatives
collisions_and_debt.action: Choose one whole cluster patch; do not combine alternatives.

collisions_and_debt.issue: The current guide specifies one notice at the first ambiguous record and does not describe per-record tail disclosures; reconcile it if any C1 patch lands.

X1 latches holder_ambiguity_stop at the first ambiguous holder even if can_check_chain was already stopped by an earlier invalid record. Its subsequent wording says the comparison is unassessed because of that ambiguity. The C2 table should distinguish the original stop cause from a later ambiguity, or the candidate should clarify that the holder ambiguity is an additional blocker.
